summary:
SolarSAR is an AI-powered satellite intelligence platform helping solar energy companies, investors, and solar park owners monitor, protect, and optimize their assets.

Traditional monitoring relies on manual inspections, scheduled maintenance, and drones. These methods are costly, slow, and limited in detecting vegetation overgrowth, flooding, terrain changes, and ground instability.

SolarSAR combines NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band SAR, Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 and Landsat optical imagery, NASA GEDI spaceborne LiDAR, Copernicus elevation data, and climate data (NASA POWER, ERA5) in one platform. It enables change detection, vegetation analysis, flood-risk screening, ground-stability monitoring, and interactive 3D mapping.

Using AI and real Earth observation data, SolarSAR helps users identify potential problems earlier, prioritize inspections, reduce maintenance costs, and make better-informed operational and investment decisions.

SolarSAR

Satellite Intelligence for Solar Infrastructure

Turning Satellite Data into Actionable Intelligence for Solar Energy Assets.

SolarSAR is an AI-powered geospatial intelligence platform that helps solar energy companies, infrastructure investors, and asset owners monitor, protect, and optimize solar installations using real satellite observations and advanced Earth observation technologies.

01. THE PROBLEM

Solar Infrastructure Is Growing. Monitoring Is Not Keeping Up.

Solar farms are large, geographically distributed infrastructure assets that require continuous monitoring. Yet many existing maintenance and monitoring processes remain fragmented, expensive, and reactive.

Today's Key Challenges

Expensive Manual Inspections

Field teams and scheduled drone surveys require personnel, equipment, planning, and repeated data collection.

Limited Monitoring Coverage

Frequent and consistent inspection of large solar installations is difficult and costly.

Incomplete Cleaning Solutions

Automated cleaning systems remove dust and surface contamination but cannot independently assess wider environmental and terrain-related risks.

Undetected Vegetation Growth

Overgrowth can create shading, obstruct access, and increase maintenance requirements.

Environmental Exposure

Poor drainage, flooding, terrain changes, and ground instability can threaten infrastructure and site accessibility.

Fragmented Information

Satellite imagery, operational reports, environmental data, and maintenance records are often analyzed separately.

For institutional investors and asset owners, the challenge extends beyond maintenance. Assessing the physical condition and environmental exposure of solar infrastructure requires reliable, location-specific information.

THE RESULT: Higher operational costs, delayed risk identification, and limited visibility into the actual condition of solar assets.

02. OUR SOLUTION

One Platform. Multiple Data Sources. A Complete View of Solar Infrastructure.

SolarSAR combines Earth observation, geospatial analysis, machine learning, and environmental monitoring into one unified intelligence platform.

Instead of relying exclusively on manual inspections, isolated monitoring tools, or simulated scenarios, SolarSAR uses real satellite observations and documented geospatial datasets to identify changes and potential risks across solar installations.

SolarSAR Helps Users Understand:

  • What is changing across a solar installation.
  • Where potential environmental and infrastructure risks are emerging.
  • Which locations require further investigation.
  • How site conditions evolve over time.
  • Where inspection and maintenance resources should be prioritized.

Our objective is to transform satellite observations into actionable intelligence for operational and investment decisions.

03. NASA & EARTH OBSERVATION TECHNOLOGY

Powered by Real Satellite Observations

NASA NISAR is a central scientific component of SolarSAR.

Its Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) technology provides observations of the Earth's surface regardless of daylight and, within suitable operating conditions, through cloud cover.

These observations can help identify changes in radar backscatter and, where appropriate data and processing are available, surface displacement and ground-stability patterns.

SolarSAR aims to compare observations acquired at different dates over the same solar installation, identify measurable changes, and visualize relevant results through an interactive geospatial interface.

Integrated Earth Observation Datasets

NASA NISAR

L-band SAR observations for satellite-based change detection and ground-stability analysis where appropriate.

Sentinel-1

C-band SAR time series for historical radar monitoring, surface-change analysis, and anomaly detection.

Sentinel-2

Optical satellite imagery for vegetation monitoring, land-cover classification, and environmental change detection.

Landsat 8/9 & ECOSTRESS

Long-term optical observations and land-surface temperature monitoring.

GEDI LiDAR

Spaceborne laser observations providing vegetation structure and height information where measurement footprints are available.

Copernicus DEM

Terrain elevation, slope, and drainage-related analysis.

NASA POWER & ERA5

Environmental and climate information, including solar radiation, precipitation, soil moisture, temperature, and wind.

OpenStreetMap

Geographic information covering roads, buildings, surrounding infrastructure, and other relevant features.

DATA TRANSPARENCY IS FUNDAMENTAL TO SOLARSAR.

Each dataset is presented with its source, acquisition date, and relevant limitations. The platform distinguishes actual satellite observations from derived indicators, forecasts, and illustrative demonstration data.

04. KEY PLATFORM CAPABILITIES

Six Intelligence Modules. One Integrated Platform.

01 — Satellite Change Detection

Detect What Has Changed. Identify Where Attention Is Needed.

SolarSAR compares satellite observations across different dates to identify changes around solar installations.

Capabilities Include:

  • SAR backscatter comparison.
  • Historical satellite observation analysis.
  • Identification of potentially anomalous areas.
  • Visualization of changes on interactive maps.
  • Isolation Forest machine-learning anomaly detection against historical site baselines.

The objective is to help operators identify locations that may require further investigation.

02 — Vegetation & Land Monitoring

Understand the Environment Surrounding Your Solar Assets.

Using Sentinel-2 imagery and available LiDAR observations, SolarSAR analyzes vegetation patterns and environmental changes around solar parks.

Capabilities Include:

  • Vegetation monitoring.
  • Land-cover classification.
  • Identification of vegetation growth patterns.
  • Monitoring of areas around and between panel rows.
  • Random Forest classification trained using Sentinel-2 and ESA WorldCover data.

These insights help prioritize vegetation management and reduce unnecessary field inspections.

03 — Ground Stability & Flood-Risk Screening

Identify Potential Environmental Threats Before They Become Operational Problems.

SolarSAR combines radar observations, elevation models, terrain slope, and environmental datasets to screen for potential infrastructure risks.

Capabilities Include:

  • Ground-change monitoring.
  • SAR-based surface displacement analysis where suitable.
  • Terrain elevation and slope assessment.
  • Potential flood-exposure screening.
  • Drainage-related risk indicators.
  • Environmental condition monitoring.

These outputs support risk identification and further investigation. They are not replacements for engineering surveys, geotechnical assessments, or certified flood studies.

04 — Solar Infrastructure Intelligence

A Unified Overview of Solar Park Conditions.

SolarSAR brings multiple monitoring layers together to help operators understand the wider condition of their installations.

Capabilities Include:

  • Site-wide environmental monitoring.
  • Identification of potential operational risks.
  • Historical condition comparison.
  • Maintenance prioritization.
  • Geospatial infrastructure analysis.

Future development will explore integration with inverter and SCADA data to connect satellite-derived indicators with actual plant performance.

Satellite observations alone cannot confirm individual panel failures or electricity production.

05 — Interactive 3D Digital Twin

Explore Your Solar Infrastructure from a Completely New Perspective.

SolarSAR features an interactive 3D geospatial environment built using MapLibre and OpenStreetMap data.

Users Can:

  • Explore solar installations in 2D and 3D.
  • Visualize surrounding infrastructure and roads.
  • Examine terrain elevation and geographic features.
  • Switch between analytical map layers.
  • Inspect specific locations.
  • Compare available satellite-derived information.

The 3D environment provides an intuitive way to understand the spatial relationships between solar infrastructure and its surrounding environment.

06 — Investor & Portfolio Intelligence

Better Visibility. Better-Informed Investment Decisions.

SolarSAR is designed not only for operational teams but also for financial decision-makers.

Investors and Portfolio Managers Can:

  • Review environmental exposure.
  • Monitor changes across multiple solar assets.
  • Identify potential site-specific risks.
  • Access consistent geospatial information.
  • Support asset due diligence.
  • Improve portfolio monitoring.

This creates an additional layer of independent, location-specific intelligence for renewable energy investments.

05. TARGET CUSTOMERS & BUSINESS MODEL

Built for the Renewable Energy Investment Ecosystem.

SolarSAR follows a B2B subscription-based business model, targeting organizations that own, operate, maintain, finance, or evaluate solar infrastructure.

Primary Customer Segments

01. Hedge Funds & Institutional Investors

Investment organizations that own, finance, or evaluate renewable energy infrastructure and require independent information about asset conditions and environmental exposure.

02. Large Private Solar Park Owners

Companies and private investors managing one or multiple solar installations who need reliable monitoring and risk assessment.

03. Solar Farm Operators

Businesses responsible for daily operations, performance, maintenance, and long-term infrastructure reliability.

04. Solar O&M and Maintenance Companies

Service providers seeking to optimize field inspections, vegetation management, and maintenance activities.

05. Renewable Energy & Infrastructure Investment Managers

Organizations responsible for monitoring and evaluating portfolios of renewable energy assets.

Revenue Streams

Recurring Software Subscriptions

Subscription-based access to SolarSAR's monitoring and analytical platform.

Portfolio Monitoring Packages

Monitoring solutions for organizations managing multiple solar installations.

Asset-Specific Risk Reports

Detailed geospatial and environmental assessments for individual solar parks.

Enterprise Platform Access

Customized solutions for larger organizations and institutional customers.

Custom Integrations & Data Services

Integration with existing operational systems and specialized data services.

Our business model is designed around recurring revenue and scalable monitoring across multiple solar installations.

06. ECONOMIC & OPERATIONAL VALUE

Turning Better Monitoring into Measurable Financial Value.

SolarSAR is designed to create economic value through earlier risk identification, targeted inspections, improved maintenance planning, and better-informed investment decisions.

Expected Operational Benefits

Reduced Inspection Costs

Fewer unnecessary manual inspections and drone surveys.

More Efficient Maintenance

Better allocation of maintenance personnel and resources.

Earlier Risk Identification

Earlier identification of vegetation and environmental risks.

Improved Operational Planning

Better-informed maintenance decisions based on site-wide environmental conditions.

Reduced Operational Exposure

Improved visibility into potential flooding, drainage, and ground-stability concerns.

Better Investment Due Diligence

More consistent geospatial information for renewable energy portfolios.

Resource Optimization

Improved planning of maintenance resources through future operational data integration.

The Economic Opportunity

According to the IEA Photovoltaic Power Systems Programme, global PV energy-production losses associated with soiling were estimated at approximately 3–5% in its 2023 report. Its 2025 fact sheet reports global average losses of approximately 4–7%.

These figures illustrate the scale of potential production losses across the solar industry. They are not savings that SolarSAR can automatically recover. SolarSAR does not currently measure panel soiling directly.

Illustrative 100 MW Solar Farm Scenario

INSTALLED CAPACITY

100 MW

ANNUAL ELECTRICITY GENERATION

150 GWh

ELECTRICITY VALUE

€60/MWh

ESTIMATED ANNUAL REVENUE

€9,000,000

ILLUSTRATIVE PRODUCTION LOSS

3–5%

POTENTIAL ANNUAL REVENUE EXPOSURE

€270,000–€450,000

This example demonstrates the potential financial significance of production losses in large solar installations.

It is an illustrative scenario, not a measured result for a particular solar park. Not all production losses are recoverable through satellite monitoring.

SolarSAR will evaluate potential economic benefits using asset-specific information, including installed capacity, electricity generation, energy prices, maintenance costs, inspection frequency, and verified operational outcomes.

07. WHY SOLARSAR?

More Than Satellite Monitoring. A Complete Geospatial Intelligence Approach.

SolarSAR is not designed around a single maintenance activity or one satellite dataset.

Its core differentiation is the integration of multiple Earth observation sources, environmental information, and machine-learning analysis into one unified geospatial intelligence platform.

Traditional Monitoring Approaches

Periodic Manual Inspections

Monitoring often depends on scheduled physical inspections and personnel availability.

Separate Monitoring Tools

Different systems provide isolated information about individual operational activities.

Limited Environmental Visibility

Wider environmental and terrain-related risks may remain outside standard maintenance processes.

Reactive Maintenance

Problems may only receive attention after they have affected operations.

Fragmented Asset Assessments

Information about different solar installations can be difficult to compare consistently.

The SolarSAR Approach

Satellite-Based Monitoring

Analyze available observations over time to identify changes across solar installations.

Unified Geospatial Intelligence

Combine multiple satellite and environmental datasets in one interface.

Integrated Environmental Analysis

Connect vegetation, terrain, flooding, and ground-stability indicators.

Data-Driven Inspection Prioritization

Help operators identify locations that may require additional attention.

Multi-Asset Portfolio Monitoring

Provide consistent geospatial information across multiple renewable energy assets.

SolarSAR is designed to complement existing cleaning systems, drone inspections, maintenance operations, and SCADA infrastructure.

WE DO NOT AIM TO REPLACE EVERY PHYSICAL INSPECTION. WE AIM TO MAKE EVERY INSPECTION MORE INFORMED, TARGETED, AND VALUABLE.

08. OUR VISION

Protecting the Future of Solar Energy Through Satellite Intelligence.

The global renewable energy sector is expanding, and solar infrastructure is becoming an increasingly important part of the world's energy system.

As solar portfolios grow, the need for reliable, scalable, and independent infrastructure monitoring will become increasingly important.

SolarSAR aims to make solar infrastructure monitoring more proactive, data-driven, and financially transparent.

By combining NASA Earth observation technologies, satellite imagery, geospatial intelligence, and machine learning, we aim to help solar companies protect their infrastructure, reduce avoidable operational costs, and make better decisions.

For investors, SolarSAR aims to provide a clearer understanding of the real-world condition and environmental exposure of renewable energy assets.

SolarSAR

See Beyond the Panels. Understand the Ground. Protect the Investment.
